stemMd: Which blood vessel normally carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
explanationMd: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Vessel names refer to direction relative to the heart: veins lead toward it and arteries lead away. Oxygenation alone therefore does not determine whether a vessel is an artery or a vein.

distractorRationale.d: The pulmonary artery carries blood from the heart toward the lungs.
distractorRationale.e: The vena cava returns systemic venous blood to the right atrium.
distractorRationale.b: The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the systemic circulation.
distractorRationale.c: The portal vein carries blood from the digestive region toward the liver.
